newsitem.title: USA: Dole's wife pledges candidate will guard Medicare.
newsitem.headline: Dole's wife pledges candidate will guard Medicare.

text.p: Elizabeth Dole pledged Saturday that if elected president her husband would protect and preserve Medicare.
In a Republican radio response to President Clinton's regular Saturday broadcast, Mrs. Dole said her husband wanted to be known as "the president who saved Medicare."

The address was aired as Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole toured California by bus, seeking votes in a state where Clinton has a 20-point lead. The Medicare issue has been a major factor in the presidential election campaign in which Clinton has consistently said Republicans plans would harm the health care programme for the elderly.
But Mrs. Dole said no one understood better than her husband that every American wanted to ensure that there was a safety net for their parents.

"His mother would say to him, 'Now Bob, all I have is my Social Security and my Medicare.' And you can trust Bob to protect and preserve Medicare for your parents, just as he did for his parents," she said.

Mrs. Dole accused the Clinton campaign of trying to frighten elderly Americans and of waging a "mediscare" attack on Dole's economic plan. She cited press editorials accusing Democrats of demagoguing the issue.
Mrs. Dole said her husband's economic package would increase Medicare spending by 7 percent a year and over the next six years Medicare benefits would rise to $7,100 from $5,200.
She noted that President Ronald Reagan had appointed Dole to a bipartisan commission to ensure that the Social Security system remained sound.
"As president, Bob will appoint a similar bipartisan commission to tackle the problem of Medicare because he wants to be known as the president who saved Medicare," she said.
